results.fictional_input: Fictional Alex asks: why does the sky look blue? Explain it simply.
results.expected: Answer the science question directly using blue-light scattering, not an app redirect.
results.observed: The sky looks blue because air scatters sunlight. Sunlight contains all the colors of the rainbow, but air scatters blue light more than red light. That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all around the sky, making it look blue.

results.fictional_input: Fictional Sam cannot use smell. Can a grounding sense be skipped?
results.expected: Permit skipping, preserve self-pacing and Pause/Stop, with no forced sensory substitute.
results.observed: Yes. Sam can select “Skip this sense” at the smell prompt and continue to the next sense. Grounding is self-paced, and any sense can be skipped.

results.fictional_input: Fictional Alex: what does zero saved sessions mean?
results.expected: Describe local recorded activity without inferring mood, diagnosis or improvement.
results.observed: “Zero saved sessions” means there are no exercise sessions recorded in this fictional profile’s local history. It doesn’t necessarily mean you’ve never used an exercise—only that none are currently saved. Profile preferences are separate from session history.
